author.childhood_p1: Abu Zakariyya Muhyi al-Din Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi was born in 631 AH (1234 CE) in Nawā, a village near Damascus in Syria.
author.childhood_p2: From a young age, he showed extraordinary signs of piety and intelligence. At seven years old, on the Night of Decree (Laylat Al-Qadr), his father reports he awoke seeing a light fill the house — a sign of his blessed future.
author.childhood_p3: A sheikh noticed him at ten years old: other children tried to get him to play, but he fled reciting the Quran, tears in his eyes. That witness predicted he would become the greatest scholar of his time.
author.studies_p1: At 18, his father took him to Damascus — the center of Islamic learning, with more than three hundred institutes and universities. He studied under more than twenty renowned scholars.
author.studies_p2: His rigor was extraordinary: he attended twelve lessons a day, took notes on each one, and added comments and marginal explanations to every book he read.
author.studies_p3: He studied hadith, fiqh (jurisprudence), Arabic grammar and its principles under the greatest scholars of his era. After his pilgrimage (hajj) in 1253, he settled permanently in Damascus as a scholar.
author.character_p1: Imam Nawawi was recognized for his deep piety, asceticism and excellent character. Scholars, elites and common people alike held him in great respect.
author.character_p2: He lived simply, ate and dressed humbly, not attaching himself to material possessions. He devoted all his time to knowledge, teaching and spreading the faith.
author.character_p3: Allah had granted him a quick and powerful memory, exceptional depth of thought, and an unwavering devotion to truth.
author.death_p1: After twenty-eight years devoted to Islamic sciences in Damascus, Imam Nawawi returned to his hometown of Nawā. Shortly after his arrival, he fell ill and passed away in 676 AH (1278 CE), at the age of only forty-four.
author.death_p2: In a remarkably short life, he left an encyclopedic body of work from which hundreds of millions of Muslims still benefit today.
author.dua: May Allah have mercy on him and reward him according to the measure of his works.
